title: Axial Seamount earthquake counts in 2021-2026 stayed within 0.7-1.1 times the 2022 exponential uplift model, but no eruption followed uplift 0.36 m above the 2015 eruption level
abstract: Question: did the 2022 exponential relation between earthquake counts and uplift at Axial Seamount (Chadwick et al. 2022, G-cubed, fitted to May 2015 - July 2021) and its eruption thresholds hold in a forward test to late 2026? Data: OOI cabled bottom pressure records (central caldera MJ03F minus eastern caldera MJ03E, times 1.67, as in the 2022 paper; to 30 September 2026) and the hourly University of Washington earthquake catalog (343,591 events, to 11 November 2026). Results: (1) The exponential count model (b = 2.91 per m) predicted 212,000 earthquakes for the observed uplift path from August 2021 to September 2026; 183,000 occurred (ratio 0.87; 0.71-1.13 by period; 0.76-0.78 in 2025-2026). (2) Uplift passed the 2015 eruption level on 13 August 2024 and was 0.36 m higher on 30 September 2026, without an eruption. (3) The per-uplift threshold of the 2022 model (1e6 earthquakes per m) gives a threshold uplift of 2.76-2.83 m; the observed 2.72 m is below it, so this forecast is not yet tested. With the same-catalog 2015 value (6.1e5 per m) the threshold was 2.60-2.66 m and passed without an eruption. (4) The measured earthquakes per m of uplift reached the 2015 value (ratio 1.08) only in March-September 2026, when uplift slowed to 0.09 m/yr while the daily rate was 0.12 of the 2015 rate. (5) From 2018 the log rate followed the log uplift rate with slope 0.91 (0.61-1.20; 60-day windows 0.87, 0.64-1.10), but in 2026 the rate did not fall with slower uplift: a model without the uplift rate forecast 2026 30-day rates better (log error 0.35 versus 0.88). (6) A hinge test found no clear change of level dependence at the 2015 level. A simple rate-and-state model with stress proportional to uplift failed. Conclusion: the exponential relation forecasts counts for a known uplift path, but neither the 2015 inflation level nor an earthquakes-per-uplift ratio is a stable eruption trigger, because the ratio becomes large when inflation slows. Limitations: no MPR drift correction, a live catalog that differs from the forecasters' catalog by a factor of about 1.6, short noisy windows, uplift data end in September 2026, and one volcanic cycle without an eruption in the test period.

display.caption: Corrected differential uplift (1.67 x MJ03F minus MJ03E, from the post-2015 low) and monthly mean earthquakes per day in the UW catalog. Blue: training period of the Chadwick et al. (2022) fit; orange: forward test. Uplift passed the 2015 eruption level (dashed) in August 2024 without an eruption.
Cumulative earthquakes since 1 May 2015 against uplift. The exponential fit to May 2015 - July 2021 (dashed) predicts the forward counts within 0.71-1.13 per period, slightly too high in 2025-2026.

182-day windows: earthquake rate, uplift rate, and earthquakes per metre of uplift relative to the same-catalog value of the last 6 weeks before the 2015 eruption. The ratio reached 1 in 2026 (and 1.8 in 2023) when uplift slowed, not when earthquakes increased.
